page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.7 GHz. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) along with AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic acceleration. Memory allocation totals 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled GPUs and no local storage, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent disks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance and high memory efficiency. The instance achieved a top-25% result in stress-ng single-core processing (3,080.07) alongside Geekbench single-core (2,003.0) and multi-core (16,534.0) scores. Extended vector execution shows strong performance in cryptographic operations (PassMark encryption score of 38,547.24) and image processing. Memory throughput delivers 75.26 GB/sec read and 55.71 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks, contributing to a top-tier PassMark memory benchmark score of 2,775.75. CPU-based small LLM inference yields 2,864.49 prompt tokens per second and 319.2 generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

The absence of local ephemeral storage requires reliance on remote storage volumes, which introduces network I/O considerations for write-heavy applications. Multi-core compute throughput places in the mid-tier for its core count, as observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (201.28 GB/sec) and multi-core stress-ng tests. However, the high memory-per-core density offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound systems that do not need expensive GPU acceleration or high local NVMe throughput.

The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise relational database backends, analytics caching layers, and medium-scale memory-intensive processing tasks.
